Luide Araújo lives in the Candeal neighborhood of Salvador and has created more than 700 works, exhibiting in the Pelourinho, the Grande Hotel da Barra, and internationally in Colombia, England, and the United States. His work celebrates the street life, architecture, and popular traditions of Salvador — figures tumbling across colorful facades, street life rendered in vivid, flattened color.

This collection holds three serigraphs: two are from the same series, and one is from a separate series — acquired individually at the museum shop as the full sets were not available. Each print is signed by the artist.

Acquired at the Museu Afro Brasil gift shop — one of Latin America’s most important museums dedicated to the African and Afro-Brazilian experience, housed in Ibirapuera Park, São Paulo. The visit was an Artist’s Way artist date, part of a personal exploration of the African diaspora across continents.
